newsitem.title: CROATIA: Agip, INA press on with Croatian gas exploration.
newsitem.headline: Agip, INA press on with Croatian gas exploration.

text.p: Croatia's oil monopoly INA Industrija Nafte and Italy's Agip SpA extended their cooperation on Friday, signing a contract with an Italian firm to build an offshore platform for gas exploration in the Adriatic.

Construction of the platform on a gas field named Ivana, the largest of four currently being prospected in Croatian waters of the northern Adriatic, will begin immediately, officials of the joint venture company INAgip told a news conference.
The contract was signed with Ravenna-based Italian firm Rosetti Marino Spa which will execute the $26.65 million deal after presenting the best offer at an international tender.
"The works will be completed by the end of 1998 or early in 1999 and the production starts then," INAgip general director Zdravko Liposcak said.
He put Ivana's expected production at 23 million standard cubic metres (scm) in the first year with an annual peak of 616 million in 2001.
Underwater gas reserves in the four fields are estimated at 12 billion scm, of which Ivana could yield around six billion. But Agip's Giorgio Pesenti described these estimates as "conservative".
"It is very likely the reserve could be higher," Pesenti told Reuters, adding that further seismic measuring would determine the exact volume of gas in the fields.
He also mentioned talks on prospecting another field, to the south of the four now under development.
INA and Agip have had a long cooperation in third countries including Angola and Egypt. The Adriatic gas project, formally launched two years ago, is their second joint venture.
Agip, which is 10 times the size of INA, has better technological expertise and currently operates around 100 offshore platforms in the Italian belt of the Adriatic Sea.
The two companies have so far invested $40 million in the gas project. They expect to spend up to $210 million and three to four more years to fully develop it, Liposcak added.
Further plans include building a two-armed pipeline for gas deliveries to Italy and the Istrian peninsula in Croatia.
Once production begins, they will each take an equal share. Agip will then sell the gas to the Italian utility Snecma and INA plans to distribute it to Croatian industry and households.
Rosetti Marino Spa will subcontract local companies such as leading Croatian shipyard Viktor Lenac for certain parts of the platform, including the jacket and living quarters.
"We believe this is the best way to operate and the most competitive one," Rosetti's area sales manager Marco Deserti told Reuters.
